title: Fruit, vegetables and the market
intro: Names vary by country more here than almost anywhere else — the same fruit can be el plátano, la banana or el banano. The Mexican and widely-understood term is given first, with alternatives in the notes.

ex.es: Me como una manzana al día.
ex.en: I eat an apple a day.

ex.es: Está a dos manzanas de aquí.

entries.note: la banana in Argentina and Uruguay, el banano in Colombia. In Spain el plátano; a cooking plantain is el plátano macho.
In Mexico el limón usually means a lime, and a lemon is el limón amarillo.
In Spain and Mexico la fresa; in the Southern Cone la frutilla.

ex.en: We bought a kilo of grapes.

entries.note: In Argentina el ananá for pineapple.

ex.es: El mango está en su mejor época.
ex.en: Mango is at its best right now.

entries.note: la palta in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Bolivia. A genuine divide.

ex.es: El aguacate se pone negro rápido.

entries.note: el jitomate in central Mexico, where el tomate means a green tomatillo.

ex.es: La ensalada lleva tomate y cebolla.
ex.en: The salad has tomato and onion in it.

entries.note: un diente de ajo is a clove of garlic — literally a tooth.
la papa across Latin America, la patata in Spain. Chips or fries are las papas fritas.

ex.en: Boil the potatoes for twenty minutes.

ex.es: Ralla una zanahoria para la ensalada.
ex.en: Grate a carrot for the salad.

entries.note: Masculine, despite some lists getting this wrong. el elote is a corn cob in Mexico, el choclo further south.

ex.en: The tortillas are made of maize.

entries.note: el ají in the Andes and the Southern Cone, el pimiento for a sweet pepper in Spain.

ex.en: For a starter I ordered a salad.

entries.note: el petróleo is crude oil. el vinagre is vinegar.
la masa is dough; hornear is to bake.

ex.en: There isn't enough flour for the bread.

entries.note: cocinar is the general to cook — see unit 12. freír is to fry, asar to roast, hornear to bake.

ex.es: Cuece el arroz a fuego lento.
ex.en: Cook the rice on a low heat.

entries.en: to chop; to sting, to bite; to be spicy

entries.note: agregar is the everyday alternative to añadir in Latin America.

ex.en: Add the salt at the end.

entries.note: la sartén is feminine in most of the Spanish-speaking world, masculine in parts of Latin America.

ex.es: Pon la olla en la estufa.
ex.en: Put the pot on the stove.
